problem: The instruction 'divide by weld strength per mm to get pitch' is technically wrong. Shear flow q is in N/mm. Dividing q by a weld strength in N/mm gives a dimensionless number, not a pitch in mm. The pitch also depends on how much weld length is laid in each pitch.
fix: State it correctly: the weld must supply q N per mm of beam length. If the weld strength is s N/mm of weld and a length L mm of weld is laid in each pitch p, then sL/p ≥ q, so p ≤ sL/q. Equivalently, the required weld length per unit beam length is q/s.

problem: The sentence 'The peak is not always at the geometric centre if the width changes' is placed right after hollow circle and box, where the peak is at the centre; it can mislead students into thinking the hollow-circle peak is elsewhere. Also, for a box section at a web level, b is the total width of the two webs, not one wall thickness.
fix: For a symmetric hollow circle or box, the peak is at the centre. Use b as the total material width at that level: 2(R − r) for a hollow circle and twice the wall thickness at a web level for a box. For unsymmetrical sections, compute Q and b at each level to locate the peak.
